I am writing to offer a collection of photographs to the Society. My father, Raymond T. Oster, was a commercial photographer in Oakhaven from 1948 until his retirement in 1985. His studio, Oster Photography, was located on Main Street for most of that time. After his death in 2019, I have been going through his negatives and prints, and I have kept what I think are the most significant images of the town and its people.

The collection consists of approximately 1,200 black-and-white negatives, mostly 4x5 inch sheet film, and about 300 mounted prints. The subjects include downtown storefronts, school portraits, church groups, the 1955 flood, the new high school construction in 1962, and many civic events such as the centennial parade and the county fair. There are also a number of unlabeled negatives that would require identification.

I am not certain of the archival value of all of this, but I would rather see it housed properly than risk it being thrown away after I am gone. My father was meticulous about labeling his envelopes, but the system he used is not always clear to me. I would be grateful if someone from the Society could look at the material and advise whether it fits your collecting scope.

I have attached a list of the major groupings. Please call me at 555-0198 or email me at m.oster@frontier.com if you would like to schedule a time for me to bring a sample of the negatives and prints to the museum.

Sincerely,

Margaret Oster

Oakhaven, OH 44870

Harold

Sarah

David

I am writing to offer a collection of photographs to the Society. My father, Raymond T. Oster, was a commercial photographer in Oakhaven from 1948 until his retirement in 1985. His studio, Oster Photography, was located on Main Street for most of that time. After his death in 2019, I have been going through his negatives and prints, and I have kept what I think are the most significant images of the town and its people.

The collection consists of approximately 1,200 black-and-white negatives, mostly 4x5 inch sheet film, and about 300 mounted prints. The subjects include downtown storefronts, school portraits, church groups, the 1955 flood, the new high school construction in 1962, and many civic events such as the centennial parade and the county fair. There are also a number of unlabeled negatives that would require identification.

I am not certain of the archival value of all of this, but I would rather see it housed properly than risk it being thrown away after I am gone. My father was meticulous about labeling his envelopes, but the system he used is not always clear to me. I would be grateful if someone from the Society could look at the material and advise whether it fits your collecting scope.

I have attached a list of the major groupings. Please call me at 555-0198 or email me at m.oster@frontier.com if you would like to schedule a time for me to bring a sample of the negatives and prints to the museum.

Sincerely,

Margaret Oster
88 Sycamore Lane
Oakhaven, OH 44870

February 18, 2026

Dear Mrs. Vance,

I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to follow up on my letter of February 12. I have not heard back from you yet, and I wanted to make sure my letter arrived. I will be traveling to Florida for the month of March, so if you would like to discuss the quilt, it might be easiest to correspond by email. My address is emarsh@oakhaven.net.

I have also located a small envelope of letters that my great-grandmother wrote to her sister during the 1890s. They are mostly about family news and church activities, but they mention the quilt project and the names of several other women in the sewing circle. I thought you might be interested in these as well, as they could provide context for the quilt’s origin.

I do not want to rush you, but I would like to know if the Society is accepting textile donations at this time. I understand that museums sometimes have to be selective, and I am happy to provide any additional information that would help with your decision.

In his donor letter, James Whitfield stated, 'I committed to donate silver locket.' Record status: current.

With best regards,

Eleanor P. Marsh

February 19, 2026

Dear Mrs. Marsh,

Thank you for your letter of February 12, which I received on February 17, and for your follow-up of February 18. I apologize for the delay in responding; we have been in the middle of our annual inventory and I have been away from my desk more than usual.

The Society is indeed accepting textile donations, and the quilt you describe sounds like a wonderful addition to our collection. We are particularly interested in items with strong local provenance, and the fact that the quilt was made and used in Oakhaven makes it a very good fit.

I would be grateful if you could send photographs of the quilt, including a close-up of the quilting stitches and any details of the fabrics. We do not require a formal deed of gift until we have accepted the item, but I can send you a sample of our standard deed form so you can review it in advance.

The letters from your great-grandmother are also of great interest. We have a small archive of nineteenth-century correspondence, and letters that mention textile production would be a valuable complement. Please include a brief description of the letters when you send the photographs.

I look forward to hearing from you. My email address is h.vance@oakhavenhistory.org, and my direct line is 555-0142.

Sincerely,
